data: Mathematics has been the language to express the laws of physics. Students doing physics must be trained in mathematics. Almost every branch of mathematics has been found useful to physicists. This course builds on the foundations laid in Mathematical Methods I and II. In these courses, ideas like tensors, complex analysis, integral transforms, and some special functions are discussed. It is not the purpose of this course to take the theorem-proof route which is of importance to mathematicians. Rather, it aims to cultivate a sense of thinking that has precision and rigour which are essential to physics, and a bent of mind to understand mathematical texts. Completing this will equip students to solve advanced problems in physics and other quantitative fields.
